content:
We need to produce a resume for Matthias Algiers. Use words with all capital letters to highlight key abilities, but ensure that words with all capital letters appear less than 10 times. So we can include maybe 5-8 capitalized words. Must wrap the entire response with double quotation marks. So output should start with a double quote and end with a double quote. Inside, the resume content. Need to ensure capitalized words (full uppercase) count less than 10.

We need to think: The resume may have sections like SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION, SKILLS. If we make those headings all caps, that counts as capitalized words. Each heading is a word? For example "SUMMARY" is one word, "EXPERIENCE" one, "EDUCATION" one, "SKILLS" one, maybe "PROFESSIONAL" etc. We need less than 10 such words. We can maybe have 5 headings in caps: SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION, SKILLS, CERTIFICATIONS. That's 5. Or we could embed capitalized ability words within sentences, like "LEADERSHIP", "PROBLEM SOLVING", etc. But we must keep total <10. Safer to just have headings in caps and nothing else capitalized fully. Ensure no other words are all caps inadvertently (like "USA", "UK", "CEO", etc). Avoid those. So we must watch for any acronyms that are uppercase. So we should avoid using "USA", "UK", "CEO", "CFO", "IT", "AI", etc. Also avoid "e.g."? That's not uppercase. So we need to be careful.

Thus produce a resume with headings in all caps: SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION, SKILLS, CERTIFICATIONS. That's 5 words all caps. Ensure no other all caps words appear. Also ensure we don't accidentally have "Mr."? That's not all caps. "Matthias Algiers" is normal case.

We need to wrap entire response with double quotation marks. So output should be:

"SUMMARY
...
"

Make sure the outermost characters are double quotes. Inside we can have line breaks. That is okay.

We must not add commentary about constraints. Just output the resume inside double quotes.

Check for any accidental all caps like "AND"? That's not all caps because it's lower. "AND" would be all caps if we wrote it uppercase. We'll avoid.

Check for "SQL"? That's all caps; avoid. Avoid "HTML". Avoid "CSS". Avoid "JS". Avoid "API". Avoid "URL". Avoid "ID". So we need to be careful not to include those. Use lowercase for those: sql, html, css, js, api, url, id.

We'll write a resume with typical content.

Let's draft:

"SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with a proven track record in project management and strategic planning. Adept at driving cross-functional teams to deliver complex initiatives on time and within budget.

EXPERIENCE
SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER | Tech Solutions Inc., 2020-Present
- Led a team of 12 engineers and designers to launch three major software releases annually.
- Implemented agile methodologies, improving delivery speed by 30%.
- Managed budgets exceeding $2M, ensuring fiscal responsibility and ROI.

PROJECT COORDINATOR | Global Innovations Ltd., 2017-2020
- Coordinated multidisciplinary projects across North America and Europe.
- Developed risk mitigation plans that reduced project overruns by 15%.
- Facilitated stakeholder communication through regular status reports and presentations.

EDUCATION
MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION | University of Chicago, 2017
BACHELOR OF SCIENCE IN ENGINEERING | State University, 2015

SKILLS
Project Management, Agile & Scrum, Budget Management, Risk Assessment, Stakeholder Engagement, Team Leadership, Data Analysis, Communication, Problem Solving, Strategic Planning

CERTIFICATIONS
Project Management Professional (PMP) | PMI, 2019
Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) | Scrum Alliance, 2018"

Now check for any all caps words besides headings. Headings: SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION, SKILLS, CERTIFICATIONS => 5.

Inside content: we have words like "Tech", "Solutions", "Inc.", "2020-Present", "Led", "team", etc. No all caps. Need to ensure we didn't accidentally write "USA" etc. We didn't. We wrote "North America" (capital N and A but not all caps). "Europe" capital E but not all caps. "University of Chicago" capital U and C but not all caps. "State University" capital S and U but not all caps. "Project Management Professional (PMP)" includes "PMP" which is all caps! That's a problem. "PMP" is an acronym, all caps. We need to avoid that. Similarly "CSM" is all caps. Also "PMI" and "Scrum Alliance" maybe "Scrum" capital S but not all caps. But "PMP", "CSM", "PMI" are all caps. Must avoid them. Also we have "Agile & Scrum" - "Agile" capital A but not all caps, "Scrum" capital S but not all caps. Good.

We need to remove or lowercase those acronyms. Could write "Project Management Professional (pmp)"? But that looks weird. Better to write out the certification without acronyms: "Project Management Professional Certification". Or we can write "Project Management Professional (Pmp)" with only first letter capital? That's not all caps. But the parentheses content would be "Pmp" which is not all caps (only first capital). That's okay. Similarly "Certified ScrumMaster (csm)". Or we could write "Certified ScrumMaster". Avoid acronyms.

Also we need to check for any other all caps like "ROI". We wrote "ROI" in the sentence: "ensuring fiscal responsibility and ROI." That's all caps. Must avoid. Change to "return on investment". Good.

Check for "AI"? Not present.

Check for "IT"? Not present.

Check for "USA"? Not present.

Check for "UK"? Not present.

Check for "LLC"? Not present.

Check for "Inc." we have "Inc." with capital I and lower nc? Actually "Inc." is capital I then lower nc then period. That's not all caps because only first letter capital. So fine.

Check for "Ltd." similarly.

Check for "MBA"? We wrote "MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION" which is all caps heading? Actually we have heading "EDUCATION". Under that we have "MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION | University of Chicago, 2017". That phrase "MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION" is all caps! That's a problem. We need to avoid that. We should write it in normal case: "Master of Business Administration". Similarly "BACHELOR OF SCIENCE IN ENGINEERING" should be normal case.

Also "SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER" is a job title; we have that as "SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER | Tech Solutions Inc., 2020-Present". That's all caps again. Need to avoid all caps in job titles. We can write "Senior Project Manager". Similarly "PROJECT COORDINATOR" should be "Project Coordinator". Also we have "GLOBAL INNOVATIONS LTD." maybe we wrote "Global Innovations Ltd." which is fine.

Thus we need to change all caps job titles and degree titles to normal case.

Let's rewrite the resume with minimal all caps: only the headings. Ensure no other all caps words appear.

We'll produce:

"SUMMARY
Dynamic professional with a proven track record in project management and strategic planning. Adept at driving cross-functional teams to deliver complex initiatives on time and within budget.

EXPERIENCE
Senior Project Manager | Tech Solutions Inc., 2020-Present
- Led a team of 12 engineers and designers to launch three major software releases annually.
- Implemented agile methodologies, improving delivery speed by 30%.
- Managed budgets exceeding $2 million, ensuring fiscal responsibility and return on investment.

Project Coordinator | Global Innovations Ltd., 2017-2020
- Coordinated multidisciplinary projects across North America and Europe.
- Developed risk mitigation plans that reduced project overruns by 15%.
- Facilitated stakeholder communication through regular status reports and presentations.

EDUCATION
Master of Business Administration | University of Chicago, 2017
Bachelor of Science in Engineering | State University, 2015

SKILLS
Project Management, Agile & Scrum, Budget Management, Risk Assessment, Stakeholder Engagement, Team Leadership, Data Analysis, Communication, Problem Solving, Strategic Planning

CERTIFICATIONS
Project Management Professional Certification | PMI, 2019
Certified ScrumMaster | Scrum Alliance, 2018"

Now check for any all caps words besides headings.

Headings: SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, ED
